digest.component_or_area: MCP error handling and CLI/library error classification
propositions: MCP tool failures currently surface errors as unstructured prose or ad-hoc partial shapes, while the CLI already emits a structured error_envelope discriminator; MCP must emit the same discriminator for agents to distinguish error types without pattern-matching English

A central error_code_for(exc)->str classifier and KNOWN_ERROR_CODES registry must be added to _errors.py as a single source of truth, classifying by exception type (not message substring) and re-exported as rebar.error_code_for so the library interface exposes machine error codes

The MCP boundary must wrap rebar exceptions in McpEnvelopeError (carrying structured .envelope dict) that raises on the ToolError.__cause__, allowing robust structured consumers to read exc.__cause__.envelope["error"] without text prefix-stripping

TicketNotFoundError must be introduced as a ReadError subclass raised only at genuine not-found sites (reads.py:310/313) with identical messages, preserving CLI byte-identity while enabling isinstance-based classification independent of message wording

MCP soft-error returns (_mcp_reads explain_criterion, _mcp_llm) must gain vocabulary error codes (criterion_unknown_id/registry_malformed/missing_file; llm_unavailable) while preserving existing agent-branching fields (kind, resolution_class, retryable, diagnostic)

A cross-interface test must verify that the same failure (missing ticket, concurrency mismatch) produces identical error codes when driven through the library error_code_for, CLI error_envelope, and MCP McpEnvelopeError, ensuring no code exists on one interface only
